Subject: API/model deprecation cascade — proposed mitigations and customer exception process

Team —

Quick summary: Product is planning a staged deprecation of the inference-v2 API surface (models inference-v2/*) with tight timelines driven by kernel/quantization improvements. Several strategic customers (notably Acme Corp) have asked for a formal exception path and documented mitigation options. I pulled together an initial timeline and two asks:

1) Can engineering confirm whether we have a supported compatibility shim for dedicated instances (so existing requests can be routed to inference-v1 for a 90-day grace period)?
2) Product needs a prescriptive exceptions workflow (criteria + approvers + comms template) for customers requiring more time.

Attached: migration_timeline_v2.xlsx (draft), comm_draft_for_customers.docx.

Explicit asks from me: can @markus confirm feasibility of the shim + @aditya/Laura can we get an approval flow by EOD next Thursday so we can tell Acme before their renewal outreach?

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jul 7, 2027 at 9:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> Quick summary: Product is planning a staged deprecation...

Thanks for the clear ask, Olga. Technical notes:

- We can implement a compatibility routing shim for Dedicated customers that preserves v2 semantics by routing traffic to a v1-compatible runtime for a limited period. Work estimate: 2 engineers x 3 weeks (includes integration tests and QA). This will not be available for hosted multi-tenant customers without capacity/configuration work.

- Two important caveats:
  * KV-cache layout changes in v2 mean regenerated prefixes will miss; some latency/cost implications expected for the shim path.
  * We need product to decide whether we support "behavioral parity" or "best-effort parity" for the grace period. Behavioral parity will require additional test coverage and likely extend timeline by ~1 week.

- For exceptions: engineering can support a short-term, technically-scoped exception (90 days) per customer. For >90 days we should require a PM/Eng/Legal sign-off and an engineering impact review.

I've attached a small redline (acme_exception_request.pdf) with the compatibility assumptions.

-Markus

Attachments: acme_exception_request.pdf (pdf, redline)

I looped in Acme (Jane) on the next message so they know we'll share the timeline and options.

-Laura
